newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan opposition rejects economic package.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan opposition rejects economic package.

text.p: Pakistani opposition parties rejected a harsh IMF-inspired economic stabilisation package on Wednesday and called for a nationwide protest general strike on Saturday.
Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government announced the package on Tuesday, including a big devaluation of the rupee and new taxes worth 13 billion rupees ($323 million).

"The whole nation rejects this package and wants to get rid of it immediately," opposition leader Nawaz Sharif told a news conference where he announced the call by his Pakistan Muslim League party and its allies for all business to strike.

"The opposition does not permit the government to punish the people for its incompetence, inefficiency and corruption," he said. "The game this government has played with the nation is a national crime and it should be punished for this crime."

On Tuesday, State (central) Bank of Pakistan governor Muhammad Yaqub announced plans to narrow the budget gap by 40 billion rupees in fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) through spending cuts, extra taxes and a 10 percent rise in fuel prices.
The bank also devalued the rupee by 7.86 percent agianst the dollar and raised its key repurchase (repo) discount rate to 20 percent a year from 17 percent.

Sharif said the package, designed to get the International Monetary Fund to resume stalled disbursements from a $600 million standby loan, would raise cost of production and make local industry uncompetitive in the international market.

He said the government had violated the Pakistan constitution by announcing the package through the central bank rather than presenting it before the National Assembly (lower house) for approval, as is done for the state budget.
"It (parliament) is not an academic debating society, it is a parliament and this package should have been brought to the parliament before its announcement," Sharif said.
